claim: Green leaf volatiles (GLVs) constitute a widespread group of defensive plant volatiles that convey a herbivory-specific message via their isomeric composition.

claim: (E)-2-GLVs and/or specific (Z)-3/(E)-2-ratios provide information regarding host plant attack by conspecifics that ovipositing hawkmoths use for host plant selection.

claim: Insects rely on olfaction in most aspects of life including locating food sources, mating partners, and oviposition hosts.
source_text: Insects rely on olfaction in most aspects of life: volatile signals guide them to food sources, mating partners and oviposition hosts
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge about insect behavior, supported by general citations.

claim: Plant volatiles provide important cues for herbivorous insects to locate and identify appropriate host plants for their offspring.

claim: Plants respond to herbivory with an increased release and de novo synthesis of several volatile compounds from their vegetative tissues.
source_text: Upon herbivory, plants respond with an increased release and de novo synthesis of several volatile compounds from their vegetative tissues

claim: Herbivore-induced plant volatile composition and abundance reflect several biotic and abiotic factors.

claim: The antennal lobe of M. sexta females consists of about 70 structural and functional subunits called olfactory glomeruli.

claim: OSNs expressing the same receptor converge onto the same glomerulus in the antennal lobe.

claim: Green leaf volatiles are characterized by a C6-backbone.

evidence_reasoning: This is a basic chemical characteristic of GLVs, established knowledge in the field.

claim: GLVs are emitted only in trace amounts from healthy, undamaged plant tissue but are emitted instantly after cell disruption.
source_text: While emitted only in trace amounts from healthy, undamaged plant tissue, they are emitted instantly after cell disruption

claim: GLVs are generated from C18-fatty acids via the enzymes lipoxygenase (LOX) and hydroperoxide lyase (HPL).
source_text: GLVs are generated from C18-fatty acids via the enzymes lipoxygenase (LOX) and hydroperoxide lyase (HPL)
evidence_reasoning: This describes the established biosynthetic pathway for GLVs, supported by citations.

claim: (Z)-3-hexenal originates from the cleavage of α-linolenic acid through the activity of HPL and partly rearranges to (E)-2-hexenal.

claim: GLVs have been assigned various plant defense-associated functions by directly inhibiting phytopathogens.

claim: GLVs are thought to act as nonspecific signals of plant damage due to their ubiquity and instant release.

claim: The herbivore-induced change in the (Z)-3/(E)-2-ratio attracted the generalist hemipteran predator Geocoris spp., which decreased the herbivore load on the plant by feeding on herbivore eggs.

claim: When comparing the two different hexenyl acetates, on average one additional egg per plant was oviposited on sides scented with the (Z)-3-isomer.

claim: OS-specific changes in the (Z)-3/(E)-2-ratio were detectable during one of the two nights in field experiments.

claim: The ratio of plant volatiles is an important component of the olfactory signal.
source_text: Numerous studies suggest that the ratio of plant volatiles is an important component of the olfactory signal
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to studies on volatile ratios.

claim: Augmenting the volatile emission of a potato host plant with single GLV components resulted in a disruption of the orientation of L. decemlineata to the potato plant.
source_text: Augmenting the volatile emission of a potato host plant with the single GLV components (Z)-3- or (E)-2-hexenol, (E)-2-hexanal or 1-hexanol resulted in a disruption of the orientation of L. decemlineata to the potato plant
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Visser and Avé, 1978.

claim: Neurons specifically responding to GLVs have been found both at the periphery and in the antennal lobe of L. decemlineata.
source_text: Further studies found neurons specifically responding to these GLVs both at the periphery and in the AL of L. decemlineata
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to De Jong and Visser, 1988a, 1988b.

claim: For the oriental fruit moth Grapholita molesta, the ratio of a minor compound to the remaining components of a plant-derived synthetic mixture determined behavioral acceptance of this mixture.
source_text: In the case of the oriental fruit moth, Grapholita molesta, the ratio of a minor compound to the remaining components of a plant-derived synthetic mixture determined behavioral acceptance of this mixture
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Piñero et al., 2008 and Najar-Rodriguez et al., 2010.

claim: Ovipositing Manduca moths distinguished between different (Z)-3/(E)-2-ratios and used these volatile cues to choose oviposition sites associated with less feeding competition and predation.
source_text: We found that ovipositing Manduca moths distinguished between different (Z)-3/(E)-2-ratios and that they used these volatile cues to choose oviposition sites associated with less feeding competition and predation
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by oviposition assay data and inferred from the ecological context.

claim: Ovipositing Manduca moths continuously preferred the side of the plant that smelled more of (Z)-3-GLVs, or less of (E)-2-GLVs, regardless of mixture complexity.
source_text: However, independent of whether the mixtures tested were rather complex in their composition (9:1 vs 1:1 ratios), or less complex (only (Z)-3-GLVs vs only (E)-2-GLVs), or consisted of only a single compound ((Z)-3-hexenyl acetate vs (E)-2-hexenyl acetate) ovipositing Manduca moths continuously made a choice and always preferred the side of the plant that smelled more of (Z)-3-GLVs, or less of (E)-2-GLVs
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by oviposition assay data across different experimental conditions.

claim: M. sexta moths learn to feed from flowers of non-hosts due to olfactory conditioning.
source_text: It has been shown that M. sexta moths learn to feed from flowers of non-hosts due to olfactory conditioning
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Riffell et al., 2008, 2013.

claim: Experience could shape female oviposition choice as it has been shown in other moth species.
source_text: Experience could as well shape female oviposition choice as it has been shown in other moth species
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative reasoning supported by citations to studies in other species.

claim: The retention of odor memory learned at the larval stage onto the adult stage has been shown to occur in M. sexta.
source_text: The retention of odor memory learned at the larval stage onto the adult stage has been shown to occur in M. sexta
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Blackiston et al., 2008.

claim: The antennal lobe has the capacity to resolve the composition of GLV blends as emitted by highly relevant host plants.
source_text: Our results show that the AL, the first odor processing center of the insect brain, has the capacity to resolve the composition of GLV blends as emitted by highly relevant host plants
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the functional imaging data showing distinct responses to different GLV compositions.

claim: Gravid Manduca females prefer oviposition sites with reduced predation and competition risks for their offspring, as indicated by the plant volatile bouquet.
source_text: Correspondingly, gravid females make an informed choice. They prefer oviposition sites with reduced predation and competition risks for their offspring, as indicated by the plant volatile bouquet
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the oviposition preference data and the ecological context of GLV signaling.

claim: The altered GLV emission might serve to reduce the number of competitors on the host plant by informing conspecific ovipositing moths that this plant is already occupied.
source_text: In this study we hypothesized that the altered GLV emission might serve to reduce the number of competitors on their host plant by informing conspecific ovipositing moths that this plant is already occupied and, possibly, receiving increased predation
evidence_reasoning: This is the hypothesis tested in the study, supported by the experimental results.

claim: Moonlight intensity may affect GLV emission in D. wrightii.
source_text: we therefore chose two nocturnal light conditions differing by moonlight intensity to examine whether light intensity affects GLV emission in D. wrightii
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the differences observed between the two night experiments with different lunar phases.

claim: The first night field experiment was conducted shortly after a new moon with 9% of the moon illuminated.
source_text: During the first night-experiment (first night, average temperature 17.6 ± 0.7°C, wind speed 1.1 ± 0.8 m/s, waxing crescent lunar illumination with 9% of the moon illuminated)
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation of the experimental conditions.

claim: The second night field experiment was conducted during a full moon.
source_text: During the second experiment (second night; average temperature 24.6 ± 0.8°C, wind speed 0.7 ± 0.8 m/s, full moon)
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation of the experimental conditions.

claim: By adding a single component to the volatile bouquet of native D. wrightii plants one can alter the choice of ovipositing Manduca moths.
source_text: From our results we cannot conclude whether a complex GLV bouquet of different ratios provides more reliable information than do single compounds, but our results demonstrate that by adding a single component to the volatile bouquet of native D. wrightii plants one can alter the choice of ovipositing Manduca moths
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by the oviposition assay results with single compounds.

claim: M. sexta larvae feeding on plants are continuously surrounded by GLVs emitted from wounded plants.
source_text: A M. sexta larva feeding on plants, however, is continuously surrounded by GLVs emitted from wounded plants
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the known biology of feeding larvae and GLV emission patterns.

claim: M. sexta larvae encounter almost continuously a low (Z)-3/(E)-2-ratio caused by their own oral secretions.
source_text: and more importantly encounters almost continuously a low (Z)-3/(E)-2-ratio caused by its own oral secretions
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the demonstrated effect of oral secretions on GLV ratios.

claim: The herbivore-induced volatile blend comprises several groups of compounds such as GLVs, terpenoids and/or aromatics.
source_text: The herbivore-induced volatile blend comprises several groups of compounds such as GLVs, terpenoids and/or aromatics
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Mumm and Dicke, 2010.

claim: All tested GLVs have been shown to mediate plant-insect interactions.
source_text: all of which have been shown to mediate plant-insect interactions
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Mumm and Dicke, 2010.

claim: Almost every green plant releases GLVs upon various stress conditions.
source_text: GLVs, which were investigated in the present study, seem to play an important role in volatile 'communication' as almost every green plant releases them upon various stress conditions
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the ubiquity of GLVs in plants.

claim: Manduca moths are active during sunset and night.
source_text: This makes GLVs an important cue for ovipositing Manduca moths as they are active during sunset and night
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Theobald et al., 2010.

claim: For M. sexta females, changes in the volatile emission of (Z)-3- and (E)-2-GLVs might primarily be detected via hexenyl acetate.
source_text: This leads to the proposition that for M. sexta females, changes in the volatile emission of (Z)-3- and (E)-2-GLVs might primarily be detected via hexenyl acetate
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the isomer-specific responses observed only for hexenyl acetate.

claim: Information about (E)-2-hexenyl acetate gained by ROI 4 in a dose-dependent fashion should be most valuable at a short distance to the plant.
source_text: Information about (E)-2-hexenyl acetate gained by ROI 4 in a dose-dependent fashion should, on the other hand, be most valuable at a short distance to the plant, possibly to locate the best spot for oviposition depending on the actual amounts emitted by different plant sites or to choose among neighboring plants with different levels of (conspecific) herbivory
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative reasoning based on the dose-dependent response characteristics of ROI 4.

claim: The presence of (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate might be relevant in long-range host location and host choice.
source_text: In the case of (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate, the detected signal might also be relevant in long-range host location and host choice
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative reasoning based on the ubiquity and on-off response characteristics of (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate detection.
